data.title: Validate email addresses in a CSV
data.description: Read a CSV of contacts with columns id, name and email (all strings). Check each email exactly as given, without trimming, against this rule: it is valid if and only if it contains no space characters, contains exactly one "@", the part before the "@" is non-empty, and the part after the "@" contains at least one "." and neither starts nor ends with ".". Return "invalid_ids", the ids (as strings) of rows with an invalid email, sorted by id compared as an integer ascending, and "valid_count", the number of rows with a valid email.

data.task_spec: Read a CSV of contacts with columns id, name and email (all strings). Check each email exactly as given, without trimming, against this rule: it is valid if and only if it contains no space characters, contains exactly one "@", the part before the "@" is non-empty, and the part after the "@" contains at least one "." and neither starts nor ends with ".". Return "invalid_ids", the ids (as strings) of rows with an invalid email, sorted by id compared as an integer ascending, and "valid_count", the number of rows with a valid email.

data.reasoning: The agent fetches rows via read_csv (trying the common keyword variants for the file path, falling back to a no-argument call), then applies the validation rule literally and without trimming: reject if the email contains a space character, if it does not have exactly one '@', if the local part is empty, or if the domain part lacks a '.' or starts/ends with '.'. Non-string or missing emails are treated as invalid. Invalid ids are collected as strings and sorted by integer value (non-numeric ids sorted last by string), and valid rows are counted. Returns exactly {'invalid_ids', 'valid_count'}.

evidence: read_csv returned rows used to compute invalid_ids and valid_count

data.justification: The output exactly matches the expected invalid_ids list (sorted numerically as strings '2' through '11', correctly ordered) and valid_count of 4. The validation logic correctly checks no trimming, single @, non-empty local part, domain containing a dot not at start/end.
